research_question: Does independent LLM query expansion improve successful scientific-paper discovery over the registered hybrid baseline without unacceptable latency or provider failure?

llm_expansion.ranking: baseline and expanded-query candidate rankings fused with channel-level RRF

include: accepted live-search requests with at least one returned result
human users passing production rate limits
exclude: requests outside the preregistered corpus and deployment version
duplicate actor-query requests after the first request in a UTC day

primary_outcome.name: successful_search_at_10
primary_outcome.definition: A request with at least one click, save, or positive explicit relevance judgment among the top 10 exposed results within 24 hours.

secondary_outcomes: CTR@10 using unique document clicks divided by impressions
save@10 using unique saves divided by impressions
positive explicit relevance rate among judged impressions

sample_size.stopping_rule: Stop only when both arms reach 1700 eligible requests; no unregistered interim efficacy stopping.

analysis_plan.primary_model: difference in successful-search proportions with 95% Wilson confidence interval
robustness: cluster-robust logistic regression by keyed actor digest
analysis_plan.missing_feedback: Missing explicit judgments are not treated as non-relevant; judgment rate is reported by arm.
analysis_plan.multiple_testing: Primary outcome is unadjusted; secondary outcomes are descriptive with Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted q-values.

required_artifacts: LLM provider, model, and immutable revision when available
daily arm counts and exclusion counts
